mission_1.title: Introduction: The Rise of Affrancia
mission_1.briefing:
## CHAPTER i: THE RISE OF AFFRANCIA

In the early age of kings, the region of far west was but a collection of tribes and early feudal 
chiefdoms. Among them was the chiefdom of Affrancia, a city state of the Affranc tribe, located in 
the valley of the same name, at the banks of river Euve.

Leader of this tribe, Lalenfor, son of Lalentor, was an especially power-hungry man. He saw the fields 
of Damlére and the coasts to the north and pictured the lands inhabited by his tribesmen, no longer 
limited by the rolling hills around the Euve. 

His priests, following the mighty god of thunder and rains, encouraged him. He had the favor of the 
gods, he had the  will of his ancestors. Soon, the lands he desired for his people shall be his.

He only needed one more thing - an army.

## MISSION OBJECTIVES:

- aSSEMBLE AN ARMY AND TAKE CONTROL OVER THE FAR WESTERN COAST.
mission_1.lore:
The valleys around the Euve granted many peoples from the far west shelter, land and enough 
resources for not just survival, but for establishing thriving communities. Many tribes attempted to 
coexist somewhat peacefully around the Euve, only distrubed by several days of brief conflicts a year.

This dynamic created an environment, where militant communities would eventually gain 
dominance over the peaceful ones. First of these, the Affrancs, seized their opportunity in the early 
Age of Kings by subjugating several of the adjacent tribes; the Luns, the Veligons and the Santarians. 
These tribes, wholly unprepared for the opportunism of the Affrancs fell quickly and paved the way 
for the Affranc kings to build a dominion over the riverlands.

First of these warmongering chiefs was Lalenfor, often called the First Affrancian King, who, guided 
by his retinue of thunder priests, utilized the peaceful ways of the surrounding tribes for his own gain. 
He, along with other power-hungry individuals of the tribe, exploited minor local conflicts to 
escalate a large scale war among the individual tribes. Soon, the Affrancs found themselves in an 
all-out war that claimed the lives of not only the First King, but also of many of his followers. In the 
end, however, standing upon the pile of ashes and death, the Affrancs emerged victorious and began 
to shape the destiny of the far east by the hands of Larenfor's son, Larentan.

larentan's actions took the east by storm. After his father's triumph over the north, he looked 
downwards and westwards. He knew, that the tribes of the Damlére region, situated at the very edges 
of the great Avar Deserts, were too fortified and too centralized to take on. Only one fight took 
place between the Affrancians and the Damlérians - the infamous battle of the Blue Fort, that ended 
in decimation of the Damlérian attack. After that, the western tribe began to fall into a 
self-destructive spiral and Larentan knew, that he only had to wait for his western enemy to dissipate.

He, however, had plans for territories to the south. The uplands, as the territory was called at that 
time and is still being called today, were rolling plains full of agricultural potential. He knew, that 
if he took control over that area and proclaimed it as Affrancian, he would be able to keep his people 
fed for years to come. 

Fortunately, the conviction of his people grew and the hunger for conquest was at an all-time high. 
Not much persuasion was needed to convince his growing army to wage another battle. Slaves from 
the northern territories, battered and weakened from what was at this point years of intensive labor, 
were conscripted to fight in the front lines. The Veligons, the tribe that was calling the Uplands 
their home, were a peaceful folk, that were ill-prepared for the ruthless Affrancian onslaught. 

Several battles were fought, but the bloodiest one was near the fortified city of Enire. This was the 
first battle, that Larentan was forced to abandon, as the citizens barricaded every entrance to the 
city and entrenched themselves almost impenetrably. After days of useless assaults, Larentan forfeited 
and took his army away. The city was not in his sights - the lands around it were. And the Uplands were 
all his, except for this piece of entrenched rock.

There was one final challenger that took Larentan's ire. The Santarians, people of subavarian origin 
that migrated to the far east years ago, began assembling a force to defend themselves against the 
raging Affrancian onslaught. Larentan knew he had to act swiftly. He took his force and assaulted 
the Santarians in the fields, ruthlessly murdering their population in an effort to force their chiefs 
to surrender. The chiefs, however, safely behind the walls of their major city of Auverne, put little 
heed to these calls. Soon, Larentan was forced to be content with at least additional territory
under his control.

However, the Santarians and the Veligons were not defeated. Hidden in their cities, they prepared for 
their moment to  rid themselves of the Affrancian oppressors. And their moment came just years 
after Larentan's death during the reign of his brother, Larondir.
mission_1.objectives:
## Primary Objectives

- Establish a working economy

- Train an army to protect your homeland

- Take over the hostile enemy tribes

- Follow the footsteps of the Affrancian Warlords and establish the Kingdom of Affrancia
mission_1.characters:
## Lalenfor, the First King

Lalenfor was the first of many chieftains that  revolutionized their tribe and their environment 
in ways previously thought unbelievable. His vision of the grand Affrancia was a powerful driver of 
his hunger for power - importantly, he was not motivated by his people's needs, it was his personal 
desire for power and control. Compounded by the belief of correctness of his doing, provided by the 
priests of mighty Thunder god, who saw this as the opportunity to spread their faith, this drive was 
soon put into reality by Lalenfor's lesser chiefs, who used minor skirmishes as excuse for a major war. 

Lalenfor himself was present in only one battle of the entire conquest - the battle of the Landen - 
where his overconfidence in victory caused his death; an arrow found its way into his eye. He was 
soon succeeded by his son, Larentan, who shared his father's thirst for greatness.


## Larentan, the subjugator

Larentan was the firstborn son of Lalenfor, the affrancian chieftain. He assumed control over the 
tribe a week after his father's glorious funeral and quickly took action. He, very much like his father, 
believed, that his tribe was destined to rule the entire known world. He knew, however, that to 
achieve their ultimate goal, they needed resources and food.

After dealing with the Damlérian incursion into his newly acquired territory, Larentan turned his 
gaze south, into the rich lands of what is today South Affrancia. He led his troops with conviction 
and vigor, and he was known as a very great warrior, especially with his great axe. He was spotted 
cleaving at least three Santarian warriors at once and legend says, that after this act of domination, 
Larentan took their heads and threw them at the rest of their army.

After conquering the southl Larentan attempted to consolidate power. However, his efforts were 
thwarted by constant raids from strongholds of Enire and Auverne, that sew terror into hearts of
his subordinates. Larentan was never able to bring the remaining enemy tribes to heel and died at the 
age of 46, childless, passing the mantle of leadership to his unworty brother, Larondir.

mission_2.title: Chapter 2
mission_2.briefing:
## CHAPTER ii: EARLY EASTERN CONQUESTS

While the storms gather on the western coasts of the continent, the southeastern plains of
elletian peninsula have been ever more fragmented among many small tribes. The horse-breeding
Lobards and the fisherman tribe of Ells have had powerful trading ties and sometimes even
alliances.

This all changed when a powerful individual known as Venderfornet began unifying the various
Lobard factions into a single unit via polyamorous marriages or beating his competitors into
submission with his powerful dueling skills. Soon, the house of Venderfornet emerged as the prime
lordship house of all the Lobardic tribes, centered in the region of Lobardia's capital city of Amroza.

Venderfornet and his ever-expanding sonship was not satisfied with the amount of riches currently
at his family's disposal. They began eyeing not only the peaceful Ells to the south, but also the farmers
of the Heilonic tribes and the militaristic Valeonians to the north.

Soon, the entire southeast would be engulfed by what is in today's history known as the period of
Lobardic Wars - a crusade by the House of Venderfornet to decimate his foes for blood and glory.

## MISSION OBJECTIVES:

- Defeat the Elletic Tribes

- Defeat the Heilonic Tribes

- Defeat the Chiefdom of Valeonia
mission_2.lore:
The period of Lobardic wars was a hundred-year period when the nations of the southeastern
peninsula were threatened, subjugated and conquered by the mighty tribe of Lobards. These wars
at their very start came from ambition of the house of Venderfornet, famous for the horseriding
and dueling skills of its male descendants. 

First Lobardic War, ensuing during the reign of the prime lord Venderfornet of Lobardia, was a
largely isolated conflict that had long-lasting consequences. Military supremacy of the Lobards
against the largely peaceful Ells culminated in decisive victory for the Lobards, who took over
the entire regions of Lentria and the Elletic homeland of Elletia, securing their supremacy over
the whole southeastern coastline. Major cities such as Nordariel or Lemorn were pillaged and
their riches sent over to the twin cities of Forza and Amroza to be venerated as property of the
mighty house of Venderfornet. The Lobards, however, lacking knowledge in seafaring ways, the
Lobards were never able to take complete control over the Elletian isles to the southeast. Those
have remained a firm bastion of Elletic culture for centuries.

The war was not yet over, though, as the Lobards were not satisfied. They soon stormed the
dominantly Elletic city of Neimer, always considered to be the holiest city of the world and the
seat of the Divine Mother. The razing of Neimer has become infamous for its brutality and the
plunder filled the Lobards' coffers for generations, while the city remained in ruins for long time.
The first Lobardic war was over; a decisive Lobardic Victory.

Not even a decade after, though, the next target has been painted by the warhungry Lobards.
Even though chief Venderfornet has died few months beforehand, his sons' thirst for gold has
not been quenched. Both of the north-bordering tribes - The Valeonians and the Heilons - had
military history and therefore were worthy adversaries.

Unbeknownst to the Lobards, however, their enemies were prepared. An anti-lobard coalition was
formed between the Heilons and the Valeonians. Unfortunately for the coalition, its efforts were
in vain, as the Heilons attacked faster than the Valeonians were able to fully mobilize.

Seizing this opportunity and finding an overstretched enemy, the Lobardic cavalry smashed
through the Heilonic lines and forced the Heilonic Kingdom of Worham to surrender a third 
of their territory and half of their fortune to their conquerors. The Lobards, once again 
victorious, learned of the Heilons' coalition with the Valeonians.

Expecting a strike from the west, the Lobards attacked first. They passed the valleys near occiante
and assaulted the under-defended eastern flank of the region of Valeonia. The Valeonians 
executed a well-performed withdrawal from many of their major cities, even forfeiting their
capital of Rossenburg. Soon, an armistice was negotiated between the three tribes, wherein the
Lobards were awarded large swathes of land to be added into their sphere. Soon, the chiefs of
the mighty tribe started to style themselves as Emperors - creating the very first Empire of the
world, the Lobardic Empire.

Their victories, however, did not last for long. The third and final Lobardic war saw the 
resurgence of Valeonians, Heilons and the Ells in a powerful three-way alliance, which caused
the Lobards to be surrounded on all sides. The overstretched Empire fell in few weeks of intense
fighting and the house of Venderfornet was dethroned.

The final battle took place between the Valeonian-Heilonic alliance against the Lobards near
the walls of Amroza, the Lobardic capital. The siege lasted two weeks and the city was seized from
within, as the starved population overthrew their royalty and all loyalists. 

The Third Lobardic war saw an empire toppled - with major new players emerging from its ashes -
the unified kingdom of Heilonia, spanning the heilonic kingdoms of Worham and Entaron,
the Kingdom of Valeonia, centered in Rossenburg and the Holy Kingdom, centered in Neimer 
and encapsulating the remnants of Lobardic peoples and various Elletic tribes, unified in their
reverence of the Divine Mother.
mission_2.objectives:
## PRIMARY OBJECTIVES

- Defeat the Elletic Tribes

- Defeat the Heilonic Tribes

- Defeat the Chiefdom of Valeonia

## NOTES

- Defeating the Elletic Tribes will signal the Heilonic Tribes that the war is soon upon them

- Defeating the Heilonic Tribes will trigger a retaliation from their ally, the chiefdom of Valeonia

- The Elletic Tribes will become alarmed if you mobilize too large of an army
mission_2.characters:
## Prime Lord Nogail Venderfornet

The life of Nogail Venderfornet is in many ways shrouded in mystery. He is known to be born into
a family of four brothers, each of whom demanded a piece of control over the Lobard tribe fortune
and people. 

This division shaped most of Nogail's early life. With him being the youngest of the brothers, he was
allocated the smallest amount of fortune and control - and it was being chipped away from him
constantly by his brothers. Nogail, however, used this to fuel his motivation for unification and
thirst for power.

In his eighteenth moon dance, Nogail challenged one of his brothers for a mighty duel for power
and subsequently beat him, causing his people to run to Nogail for protection. He also stole all of
his brother's fortune and wives. In the following years, Nogail hunted all of his brothers and enacted
his justice upon them. Unwittingly, he unified the Lobards under one banner.

His thirst for power has not yet been quenched. He led additional campaigns into territories of
the neighboring tribes and successfully enlarged the Lobardic empire, gathering much wealth
in the process. His greatest conquest was the plunder of the city of Neimer. which has long been a
place of culture and history of the southeast. 

## Iligano Venderfornet

The firstborn son of Prime Lord Venderfornet, Iligano was a rash and impulsive commander. Though
he was mighty with his battle polearm and a skilled horse rider, he lacked the tactical prowess
of his father. Iligano did not participate in many of his father's conquests, including the raze
of Neimer, which fueled his insecurities, that his father was not proud of him.

After the Prime Lord's death, Iligano was convinced by his younger brother, Tadeo, to share power.
He, however, demanded full command of the Lobards' mighty cavalry, which he used excessively
to conquer more land for the Lobardic Empire. Under Iligano's rule, the Lobardic Empire grew
to threaten the kingdom of Valeonia and the Heilonic tribes on their northern frontier and
even beat them in the Second Lobardic Wars.

Iligano met his end early, even before his twenty-first moon dance. He was shot in the throat by
a Valeonian archer during a battle near the fortress of Ferburg - passing the absolute power into
the hands of his brother.

## Tadeo Venderfornet

The secondborn son of Prime Lord Venderfornet, Taedo has never been excited for a man-to-man
combat. He preferred to sit in the back, giving commands to his older brother and his army from
the safety of his hut. This did not win him much glory, however, and Taedo has been largely
frowned upon by the Lobardic people.

Upon his brother's death, Tadeo became the sole ruler of the Lobardic Empire, gaining all of his
brother's fortune and wives. Under Tadeo's leadership, the Empire prevailed in the Second Lobardic
War and crushed the Valeonians in the battle of Rossenburg and the Heilons in the battles of 
Entaron and Worham, solidifying the Empire's power.

Tadeo's death, however, marked a decline in the Lobardic Empire's power. As he died childless, many
warlords struggled for power, which enabled the newly-formed alliance between the Elletic
Tribes, Valeonia and the Heilonic Tribes to attack and successfuly bring the empire down, reducing
the Venderfornet's legacy to nothing but stories in history.

mission_3.title: Chapter 3: Western Expansion
mission_3.briefing:
## CHAPTER iii: STORMS ABOVE THE WEST

The supremacy of the Kingdom of Affrancia along the western coasts has remained undisputed
for decades. After the timely conquests and unions with the surrounding kingdoms, notably
Auverne, Vense and the empirate of Carnae, their iron grip choked the east.

The only target in their minds were two island nations that occupied the pair of isles to the
northwest. The Noxeterrans, a small but military group of tribes living on the isle of Arcessa and
the Kerunians, living on the isle of Kerune. The king of Affrancia sent his best general, Serthus
Diarcess, to subjugate them..

Serthus, dissatisfied with the growing incompetence and corruption in the Affrancian nobility,
had other plans. Peacefully seizing the islands, he defected with army loyal to him and established 
a new entity - the Zjoal Kingdom, with himself on the throne.  Seeing this betrayal, the kingdom of 
Affrancia branded him a traitor to the crown and began to amass forces to dethrone him.

The new ruler of Zjoalia, however, had ambitions to turn the kingdom into an Empire. And soon, his 
plan would be set into motion.

## MISSION OBJECTIVES:

- Defeat the Kingdom of Affrancia

- Defeat the Warlords of Nordia

- Serthus must survive in Zjoal Islands
mission_3.lore:
The decades after the initial Affrancian conquests have been good for the people of the newly
dominant kingdom. While the initial chiefdom died out, the new leaders of affrancia, the house
of Duvent, declared themselves and kings and sought to unify their grip of strength along the
eastern shores, north to south.

The city of Enire, pressured by the growing military of the Kingdom of Affrancia, signed an
armistice with the new king and agreed to be formally incorporated into the kingdom. The
subsequent Raze of Enire has been a tragic event, when the victorious force enacted vengeance
upon the long-resisting town, walked through the open gates and proceeded to ransack it,
leaving nothing but fire and ash in its wake. Enire, now a shadow of its former self, became a minor
town, surrounded by a choke of empty battlements.

Auverne, however, was advancing its military even faster than the kingdom of Affrancia. The marches
of Auverne were fortified and supplied well, maintaining its power and independence in the shadow
of a superpower. Affrancian victory here was not achieved by military power - instead, it was 
won by politics. King of Affrancia, Nalemos Duvent, sought to utilize a weapon of bestowed 
marriage upon the old duke of Auverne, who lacked a male heir, only having a daughter. The duke,
not wanting to leave the future of his lands in uncertainty, signed this pact and soon, the duchess
of Auverne became the Queen of Affrancia. This union was praised across the kingdom.

It has also created a precedent. Just two generations after the union of Auverne and Affrancia,
a new kingdom has joined into a triple union - the kingdom of Vense. Vense, being a desert state
with lack of resources, but a powerful military and skilled leadership, saw its future as being
integrated into the great Affrancian union as a way of surviving in a world, where no small
nation is allowed to exist. This trend echoed across the world as a whole, not just in the east -
that the great kingdoms and empires are destined for survival - not the little tribes.

And especially in the east, at first, the first victims of this rise of imperialism appeared. A grand
crusade, with forces of Auverne, Affrancia and Vense taking up a common banner, marched
south and swiftly occupied the coastal lands of ancestral Oric tribes - Orlais and Orhas. The
marshlands of Cualus were also taken over - and cities there suffered plunders and other crimes
of war. The Affrancian advance was stopped only at the borders of another empire, that grew
in the lands of Subavaria and within the Avar Desert itself - the Uhmayyan Empiurate.

The Affrancians and the Uhmayyans signed a deal of cautious peace - setting up fortifications in
the borderlands. This was meant to be a permanent solution, but both powers knew, that it
was never to last. It allowed, however, the Affrancians to focus on their northern defenses,
as they were tested by their northern neighbors - the Nordian warlods.

Lands of Nordia, unlike their neighbors to the south, was a fragmented territory ruled by many
warlords. There was no union, just temporary alliances and in-between them, many conflicts. In
recent years, however, seeing the emergence of a powerful rival on their southern flank and
despising the different Affrancian culture, the warlords signed many alliances, allowing them
to pose as a single force against the potential southern invasion.

Affrancians, however, were not interested in taking over Nordia. They found the land was
mountainous and perilous and there was a far more pressing matter to attend to - their naval
trade routes. For years now, the Affrancian shipping was a testament of power. No other power
could match the Affrancian naval strength. Except one - and this was not a power in its own
right.

It was a relatively small nation of Noxeterrans, living on the isles to the north. Their seafaring
ways were much more advanced than the already powerful Affrancian fleets. This threat caused
the kings of the union to feel endangered - if their most powerful tool is already challenged,
what else could the nations be hiding? Could they plot to steal the union from under Affrancian
grip?

They decided to strike first. They employed their mightiest general, Serthus Diarcess, who took
command of the southwards expansion as well, to assemble a mighty host and to take control
over the Noxeterrans. Serthus, however, was at this point disillusioned in the Affrancian 
supremacy. He saw the incompetence of the kings, their paranoia and their corruption, to weaken
the structure of the union both politically and militarily. He knew it was time for change.

Serthus took an army, that was absolutely loyal to him and invaded the isles. However, upon 
landing, he quickly put down arms and instead allied with the Noxeterrans, convincing them to
join him in fight against their common enemy. Serthus was declared king and established a new
kingdom of Zjoalia, uniting forces with the southern isle of Kerune, which was already pressured
by agents from Auverne.

Affrancian response was expected and quick. The union declared war against the new Zjoal
kingdom and immediately posed armies for assault. They thought that this new enemy was no
different than the ones before. This hubris and overconfidence paved the way for Serthus to build
the most powerful empire in the history of the world - the Zjoal Empire.
mission_3.objectives:
## PRIMARY OBJECTIVES

- Defeat the Kingdom of Affrancia

- Defeat the Warlords of Nordia

- Serthus in Zjoal Islands must survive

## NOTES

- The Kingdom of Affrancia will attack immediately - be prepared!

- The Warlords of Nordia remain semi-dormant until provoked or until you grow too powerful

- Capturing the borderland territory of Orhas may change the balance of power...

- Utilize abilities of Serthus from the Heroes tab to complement your army's power
mission_3.characters:
## Serthus Diarcess

Soldier, general, emperor. The name of Serthus Diacress is often spoken as the synonym for greatness.
He is often considered the man who has created the new world, the one, who dismantled the old
ways and bestowed his glorious vision upon the continent.

His beginnings, however, were humble. Coming from the desert city of Acinta in the region of
Lunedale, Serthus was born to middle-nobility - a small steward of an insignificant line. This,
however, allowed Serthus to join the army of the kingdom of Affrancia fast and acquire a more
prominent role of a unit captain.

His instincts, knowledge of tactics and drive caused his men to adore him and his campaigns to turn
out as great successes. He led the Affrancian forces into many battles, starting in small border
conflicts on their northern border and culminating with his leadership of a massive southwards
expansion campaign, when he led the combined union army to many victories and ultimately took
over the territories of Cualus, Orhas and Orlais. For this success, he was awared the rank of the
supreme commander of the Affrancian army.

His ingenuity was, however, rivaled by his ambition. He wanted more - he wanted real power. Even
though he was very popular with the army, the highest echelons of nobility started to be ever
more suspicious of his manners. When the opportunity arrived so that the supreme commander
could be sent away, he was - into a new conflict with the tribes of Noxeterra.

Serthus, however, stunned everyone with his decision to defect. He seized the Affrancian fleet,
took the army and merged it with the Noxeterrans and Kerunians and created his new kingdom,
the Zjoal kingdom. Now, as the one person with real power, he was set to redraw the world in his
image. Commanding the mightiest fleet and a massive host, he set forth - to a new dawn.

mission_4.title: Chapter 4
mission_4.briefing:
## CHAPTER IV: DOMINATION

Decades after Serthus's grand conquest and establishment of the Zjoal Empire, the world  has
fundamentally changed. Cultural and military reforms initiated by the Zjoal rulers resonated
throughout the lands and affected millions of people. 

One such land, where the cultural change was felt the most was the province of Zjoal Far East, a
colony answering directly to the Zjoal rule. It was, by many accounts, the mother empire's most
loyal province, fundamentally caused by its ruler, Regnus Aevencourne's devotion to the Thunder
God and all other Zjoal gods.

When the Zjoal Civil War began and the newly independent kingdoms took over large swaths of
the empire, Regnus and his followers became isolated and surrounded by kingdoms, that were 
considered primitive and savage, praising their false deities and insulting all that Regnus held in
such high regard.

When the mother empire failed, it was time for a new Empire. An empire, where Regnus and the Gods
would dictate the rules. The empire of Azincourne, a land where gods and men lived in harmony,
was in the reach.

## MISSION OBJECTIVES:

- Defeat the Eastern Kingdoms

- Defeat the Confederation of the Leuse

- Regnus Aevencourne must survive in Aelatania
mission_4.lore:
Internal struggles between the participants of the nobility and the royal house became ever
more apparent within the structure of the Zjoal empire as time went by. The monarchs themselves
became weaker with every generation after the reign of king Aertei, during which the empire
reached its largest territorial extent, covering the entire continental coastline from west
to east, controlled by the mighty Zjoal fleet; one of its finest military assets. Provinces of Zjoal
Nordia, Zjoal Amennia and Zjoal Far East have been established and linked to the heartland.

After the reign of Aertei, a major plague hit the Zjoal heartland and affected its core islands
very heavily, leading to a major exodus of both common folk and the nobility to previous Affrancian
lands. At this point, the western coast was very developed, with cities like Délaen, Auverne and
Avinon becoming major cultural and commercial centers. Délaen became the primary residence
of the royal house, due to its proximity to the coast.

The divide between the nobility and the royalty, however, deepened again, when the nobility
demanded larger control over military actions performed in the northern provinces, as they felt
that they were losing control, especially in Nordian peninsula. The royalty, growing ever more
paranoid of the nobles' increasing power, declined this request and instead insisted that the
colonies should be controlled centrally by the royal family. This was unacceptable by the nobles,
as they spent large fortune establishing the architecture and fundamental control over the
provinces and expected returns from this investment. After a heated debate, the nobility
was exiled from Délaen and retreated north, to the city of Avinon.

The royalty's paranoia, however, only grew in the nobles' physical absence. Distrust also
compounded, finally prompting the royal family to send a batallion to arrest the nobles in
Avinon. The nobles, however, learned of this plot and fortified the city, inciting a major
rebellion within its walls. Avinon became a hotbed of revolt and many cities, including the Free
Cities in the north, soon followed its example.

For the royal house of Diarcess, this was the proof of the nobility's malicious intentions. King
Serton I. Diarcess declared war against the nobles, at this time led by Lord Jaelin Fourcarne and
all those, that would follow them. Soon, the empire split broadly into two factions; the branch
of Kerune, later called Kerunian Empire, named after the isle of Kerune off its coast, led by the
royal house of Diarcess, and the remained of the empire, which kept the name Zjoal Empire. More
than a conflict between the two factions, it became conflict of ideals; the idea of an absolute
monarchy against the idea of shared power among many lords.

Fourcarne and his war council resided in Avinon, which quickly became besieged by Kerunian
forces. However, support from the Free cities and other economical powerhouses of the north,
such as the Zjoal Far East province, kept the city afloat. In few weeks, a major push occured, that
would force the Kerunian army southwards. At this point, an all-out war broke out between
the south and the north, which consumed also many of the colonies.

The northern provinces, including Nordia, Amennia and Far East sided with the lords, while the
southern provinces, including Subavaria, Sordia nad Befalia became aligned with the royalty.
Zjoal Empire, however, seemed to forget, that especially in the north, the peoples were largely
subjugated and kept in check by the mother empire's military power - which quickly started to
be relocated to battles in the Zjoal heartland.

This was quickly capitalized upon by the Nordian peoples. Soon, the warlords of Nordia declared
open rebellion. Starting in the region of Conda, the revolt grew into a massive campaign that 
soon saw the entire province of Zjoal Nordia dismantled and replaced by a large, but fractured
kingdom of Voobsheconda. The only territory on the whole peninsula, that was by the end of
this campaign still loyal to the Zjoal Empire was the province of Oucine on the peninsula's 
northern coast. The war between Voobsheconda and Oucine laster for another eight years, but
was at the end left inconclusive, as the Nordian kingdom became engulfed in civil war, allowing
Oucine to survive. However, as the province was abandoned by Zjoal military and in fact all ties
have been severed, Oucine declared independence from the empire after all; but kept its cultural
heritage in line with their former Zjoal masters.

The dominoes started to fall upon the Zjoal Empire, though. Lands formerly inhabited by the
Uhmayyans also declared independence. Led by empiur Ah-Tep, called the Sunborn, the Ahtep 
Empire was declared and quickly took over the entirety of Zjoal Amennia and also lands beyond.
Ahtep Empire, unlike its Nordian counterpart, kept itself together and became a major force
on the world stage.

The last remaining province was the Zjoal Far East, which did not declare independence, mostly
due to its inhabitans' devotion to the Thunder God. Led by Regnus Aevencourne, the Zjoal Far
East found itself isolated and abandoned by the mother empire. Regnus became terrified by the
image of an isolated province among kingdoms of heretics and decided to take action against
them first - to spread the word of the Zjoal Gods and to ensure, that the legacy of the Empire
would last. Regnus believed, that the Zjoal empire was gone - and it was his charge to build a
new empire in its stead. He named his empire the Empire of Azincourne - the Empire of People and
God.

Regnus took the east by storm. Eastern Kingdoms, including the Londic Kingdom and the heilonic
kingdoms of Entaron and Venexia fell to the relentless Azincournean war machine first. The
sight of their false deities and their primary goddess, the Divine Mother, drove Regnus to a frenzy.
He assaulted the holy city of Neimer after defeating the kingdoms of Lobaria and Elletia and
razed it to the ground.

At this time, seeing Regnus's rampage, the kingdoms of the vale; Valeonia, Velognia, Calessia and
Nordica met in city of Nendys, controlled by the former Kerunian colony of Befalia, and agreed
to join forces against the Azincournean threat. The Confederation of the Leuse was proclaimed,
comprising of all four kingdoms and also the newly-independent province of Befalia.

The war of the Confederation was, however, a sound victory for Regnus and his allies. His forces
fought in unity, while the confederation armies were often disjointed and disorganized. The
morale collapsed after Regnus took over the city of Rossenburg, capital of Valeonia. Soon after,
the leaders of the confederation met with Regnus and signed an armistice; exchanging their
freedom for their lives. After the Peace of Nendys agreement was signed, the Empire of Azincourne
covered the entire east of the continent with nobody to oppose them, except the vast Ahtep
Empire to their west.
mission_4.objectives:
## PRIMARY OBJECTIVES

- Defeat the Eastern Kingdoms

- Defeat the Confederation of the Leuse

- Regnus Aevencourne must survive in Aelatania

## NOTES

- Your enemies will gradually send stronger and stronger armies against you. Leverage your early
power to gain advantage

- Emphasize early game territory gain to gain access to more building plots

- Ahtep Empire is extremely powerful and wealthy, but not required to defeat

- Utilize abilities of Regnus from the Heroes tab to gain advantage
mission_4.characters:
## Regnus Aevencourne

Regnus Aevencourne was born in the heartland of Zjoal Empire, in the city of Enire. He was a
deeply pious man from the very onset of his life, training to become a priest of the Thunder
God, as his father before him. However, destiny chose a different path from him, as he was 
conscripted by the nobility of Enire to be sent into an established Zjoal colonial province in the
east to spread the word of the Thunder God as one of the leading inquisitors.

He embarked on this long voyage right before his seventeenth birthday, sailing from the city of
Délaen northwards along the Nordian coast and then across the Amtep Sea, landing in the city
of Welthorne after a month of sailing.

While in Welthorne, Regnus came into the care of local community of clerics. Deeply devoted to
the Zjoal Gods, the clerics struggled with the local population's defiane of the divine decrees,
rooted deeply in the people's distrust of the Zjoal nobility and their vanity. Regnus spent much
of his youth travelling from town to town, spreading words about the Thunder God's benevolence
and mercy, as well as his wrath towards the unfaithful.

In his thirties, Regnus became the High Priest of Welthorne, the supreme authority of the local
clergy. He communicated constantly with the High Priests of Valona, Meladar and Daurels in
effort to unify the Zjoal Far East and establish it as a foothold of Zjoal power, anchored deep in
the faith in the Thunder God. His efforts were largely successful, as soon enough, the province
was almost all unified and its peoples had the highest rates of faith across the Empire.

Regnus's situation changed when the Mother Empire began to disintegrate and Nordians, as well
as Ahtep began their rebellions, terminating all contact between the Zjoal heartland and the
Far East province. Regnus soon believed, that the Empire was lost - and that it was the sign of the
Gods, that the vanity of their nobility was punished. He assumed the role of the Thunder God's
foremost emissary, supported by the other bishops and ascended into a position of almost
absolute power in the province.

In this position, Regnus began a righteous crusade to conquer and convert the remaining
kingdoms of the east. His campaign was swift and brutal, erasing entire cultures from existence.
He and his army of devotees swept across the continent's eastern kingdoms and defeated the
Confederation of the Leuse, establishing the Azincournean Empire on their ashes.

Regnus ruled with an iron fist. He mandated spreading faith in the Thunder God, forbade usage
of local languages, spread the Azincournean literacy across the Empire and attempted to
forge one giant culture based on devotion to the Gods. His reign was marked with a lot of 
discontent, but also a massive amount of progress, as the East soon became nearly unified in many
day-to-day things, such as language, customs or rituals.

His death came when he was nearly sixty years old. Being a pious man, Regnus had no sons of his
own and his power passed on to the council of ministers, which continued in Regnus's policies.
He was buried beneath the grand citadel of Meladar's white harbor and is still being considered
as one of the most important people in Azincourne's history and the true heir of Serthus Diarcess.

mission_5.title: Chapter 5
mission_5.briefing:
## CHAPTER V: THE FIRST WAR

It has been decades after death of Regnus the Great. However, since his death, the regime in the
conquered lands of the east has nothing but worsened. Forced culture, language and
abandonment of old ways caused many people to hide their true lives from the ever-watching
eye of the Empire's military, that was hyper-focused on enforcing the new ideals.

The first impulse of rebellion came from the very southeast - in the Elletic lands. These people,
utterly devoted to the faith in the Divine Mother and resentful of their new, forced gods, have
been conducting guerilla warfare across the Azincourneans for years, originating in their
Elletic islands and soon spreading to the mainland.

That was not the only spark of revolt, though. Young nobles from the lands of the Leuse Valley
and Nordica began planning a massive revolt, that would free the lands of the former Confederation
of the Leuse and made a pact in the city of Naragon - a pact, that would light the fire of liberty
and create one of the mightiest kingdoms of the world - Naragonthid.

There was just one task left ahead - overthrow the Azincournean Empire and forge the future
of the east in freedom.

## MISSION OBJECTIVES:

- Liberate the regions of Nordica, the Leuse Valley, Valeonia, Velognia, Révia, Venexia, Lobaria,
Lentria, Elland and the Neimer Coast from the Azincourne Empire

- Elletic Rebels' capital of Elletic isles must remain standing
mission_5.lore:
The tyranny of Azincourne's militaristic and religious oppression has not wavered after death
of its first emperor. Imperial edicts, dicating the way of life, religious rituals, language and other
matters became almost a monthly occurence, forcing the nations of the east to adjust to the
Azincournean ways. The intent of these edicts was to completely dominate the nations and
erase their cultures, so that all east will be truly unified under the Azincournean thumb.

This, however, only strengthened the will of resistance among the conquered nations. The first
one to break was the southeast nation of Elletic peoples, occupying the lands of Neimer, Elland
and the Elletian isles. At first, only small signs of resistance, such as writings on the wall, were
observed, however, the military government of these lands approached these violations with such
powerful repressive measures, that soon, people began to openly question and attack their forces.

An open rebellion erupted not late after. Cities of Nordgard and Sordgard became engulfed in
vicious conflict, wherein the local population attacked Azincournean armies en masse and
brutally murdered hundreds of soldiers, displaying their heads and bloodied banners on the 
city walls to signal their victory. They chanted the war songs of the Divine Mother during these
battles as another sign of defiance against the Thunder God.

Represailles against these attacks were swift, but inefficient. Azincourne sent two battleships
full of soldiers to the islands, but the ships were seized and the army on them was slaughtered.
This brazen show of victory opened eyes of multiple other groups on the contient, that the
Azincournean Empire was not as invincible as it seemed. Elletians soon began to draw plans for
an invasion of the mainland.

One group, inspired by the Elletic victory, were the nations of the western fringes - Nordica,
the Leuse Valley, Velogia and Valeonia - briefly unified as the Alliance of Naragon. Two young
revolutionaries, Derion Royen and Alexius Brennhen were organizing multiple unrests in these
lands and soon gathered around themselves a circle of followers. After Elletic victory, the
Naragonese revolutionaries staget their own coup and led an open rebellion against the
Azincourneans in the cities of Noxefort and Nendys. Aided by local population. exhausted by
decades of Azincournean overlordship, they attacked the Empire's army and drove them east.

The two simultaneous rebellions were impossible to contain for the already stretched
Azincournean military. Their power was reserved mostly for defensive action and the population
of the Elletic peninsula and the western fringes was ready to join the rebels. The great rebellion
of Azincourne Empire, combined with the events happening on the west - the ongoing Zjoal
Civil War - and the events of Azincourne-Ahtep conflict over Amennia, became known as the
First Continental War.

After years of struggle, the Naragonese Rebels joined the Elletic Rebels and conducted the final 
battle of Occiante, after which the Azincournean grip over the east was finally broken. Due to
the magnitude of the war and the many involved parties, the first international conference
was held in Occiante to discuss the dissolution of the Azincournean Empire. The impact of this
conference was massive - the state of the Holy Land was declared around the Neimer Coast, 
separate from the newly established country of Elletia, covering the rest of the southeastern
peninsula. The Kingdom of Naragonthid, encompassing the nations of Valeonia, Velognia,
Calessia, Befalia and the Nordica, became the new great power. The kingdoms of Révia and
Venexia were established. The Holy Land, Venexia and Révia were declared as neutral countries.

The main pain point of the conference was the decision of the states to allocate the Duchy of
Daurels to remain within Azincourne proper, despite claims of Naragonthid to own the duchy.
Arguments of the Naragonese emissaries were so that they can control the mountains separating
their territory fron Azincourne for defensive purposes, but they were outvoted, as the other
nations were growing afraid that Naragonthid would become too powerful - a phenomenon,
which was fully revealed within three decades.

## PRIMARY OBJECTIVES

- Liberate the regions of Nordica, the Leuse Valley, Valeonia, Velognia, Révia, Venexia, Lobaria,

## NOTES

mission_5.characters:
## Jaest Jinhabarra

The commander of the Elletic rebellion and the primary figureheadf of the newly established
Kingdom of Elletia, Jaest Jinhabarra has always been devoted to the Divine Mother and viewed
the Azincourne-mandated edicts as the supreme blasphemy against his goddess. Before being the
rebel leader of his nation, he was detained two times by Azincournean military and he even lost
his right thumb on his hand as punishment for desecrating a statue of Regnus Aevencourne.

He was, however, persistent in his actions and his determination and speech craft allowed him to
gather a large group of followers around him. This in turn allowed him to gain influence over
multiple groups of similarly minded people, spiraling into the full-blown rebellion against the
Azincourneans on the Elletian isles. 

Jinhabarra was never a battle commander - he was a politician. He never participated in a proper
battle against the occupiers, rather controlling and solidifying his power in the background.
After the First War was over, Jinhabarra became the King of Elletia for three years, before being
deposed by his primary rival, Kronor Sanchi, the supreme commander of Elletian army.

## Alexius Brennhen

A noble from the Nordican fortress-city of Noxefort, Alexius Brennhen has always been a vocal
advocate for the unity of the Naragonese Alliance and spoke loudly against the Azincournean
Empire on multiple occassions. Alexius was vastly popular among the Nordican people, though,
and so Azincourneans were not too keen on punishing him too badly, as not to agitate the
people in the western fringes more.

This was to be their undoing. As Alexius maintained strong contact with Derion Royen of
Arcburg and together they coordinated multiple smaller uprisings across the Leuse Valley and
the Nordican lands. The duo became even more emboldened by the Elletic victory against the
Azincourneans and decided to meet up in Noxefort to launch a full-scale rebellion.

Alexius was a commended battle officer, leading campaigns across Naragonese territories and
also acting as Naragonese emissary in the Occiante conference. He, however, never wanted to
become a king, leaving the crown of Naragonthid to Royen, when the discussion arrived. Alexius
remained the ruler of Noxefort up until his death during the Second Continental War, after
which his son Darius succeeded him.

## Derion Royen

Hailing from the northern city of Arcburg, Derion Royen was at the forefront of his family's
politics from young age. Derion learned how to cruise the waves of diplomacy and politics from
his father and hs grandfather, both of which were strong supporters of the Naragonese Alliance.
He also maintained close contact with Alexius Brennhen of Noxefort and after the death of
his father and grandfather, Derion marshalled the forces of Arcburg for the cause of the
rebellion.

While not being a battle commander like Alexius, Derion was extremely important to the war effort
due to his ability to perform diplomatic actions and navigating the complex politics of the 
rebellion, keeping it afloat, even despite internal struggles and incoherence. He negotiated the
peace among the rebels and the liberated kingdoms of Valeonia and Velognia, welcoming them
into the Naragonese Alliance and paving way for the unified Kingdom of Naragonthid after the
war.

Royen was the second emissary of Naragonthid at the Occiante conference and he advocated
for the acquisition of Duchy of Daurels, primarily due to his city's close location to the border
with Azincourne. After the conference, he was crowned as the King of Naragonthid and had
one son - Leonid Royen, who became one of the most singificant people in history of Naragonthid.
